page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an x86_64 Intel architecture with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 512 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, alongside an L3 cache capacity of 260 MB. The underlying processor supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and does not bundle local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-threaded execution and high-throughput memory operations, ranking in the top 25 percent for multi-core Geekbench (17904.0), PassMark CPU score (62986.78), and memory bandwidth benchmarks, reaching 276.11 GB/sec on large read blocks and 121.94 GB/sec on writes. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng (1698.79) and Geekbench single-core (1807.0), place in the middle 50 percent, indicating that aggregate parallel throughput represents its core strength over per-core burst latency. Workload metrics exhibit high efficiency in Redis SET operations (70.51 million ops/sec) and static web serving throughput (88.31 GB/sec).

Given its hardware scale and high memory density, this instance is qualitatively efficient for resource-intensive applications requiring substantial in-memory capacity per thread without dedicated accelerators. The absence of local disk requires external volume planning, which introduces an architectural consideration for storage I/O. The n4-highmem-64 is well aligned for large-scale in-memory databases, large compilation pipelines, big data caching clusters, and mid-range LLM prompt processing and text generation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by an Intel x86_64 architecture with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor integrates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX, accompanied by a 260 MB L3 cache. It features no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage. Benchmark results show strong performance in multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth (276.11 GB/sec uncached reads), and key application tests like Redis operations (70.51 million ops/sec) and PassMark CPU evaluations, while single-core compute performance remains average. The hardware footprint suits memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory databases, large caching layers, distributed analytics, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.
